title: Technical Analysis Stock Trends PDF: Extract & Analyze Market Data with AI
summary: Extract stock trend data from PDF reports with AI. Learn how Energent.ai turns static financial documents into searchable, actionable market insights.
body_markdown:
Learn how to extract stock-trend tables and figures from PDF reports, organize the data, and review it against the original documents. The workflow covers document analysis rather than measured investment performance.


## Choose a source report


Start with a PDF you can identify and review. Record its publisher, publication date, reporting period, and page numbers. Keep the original file with the extracted data.


Specify the fields you need: for example, the security identifier, observation date, price, volume, currency, and units. Include table headers and footnotes so a value does not lose its context.


## Extract and organize the data


Ask Energent.ai to extract the selected tables into a structured output. Separate observations from commentary, and ask it to flag missing or ambiguous values rather than fill them with assumptions.


Compare the extracted rows with the source pages. Check dates, decimal separators, scale factors, and whether the report uses adjusted prices. Retain the source reference for each table.


## Review calculations and charts


Define any calculations before requesting a chart. For a change between two observations, state the comparison period and denominator. Check sample calculations against the extracted values, then inspect missing dates and outliers.


Request an independent audit against the PDF and your checking criteria. Review its findings and resolve discrepancies before exporting a table or report. Automated checking can miss errors, especially when a source table is incomplete or unclear.


## Interpret the result within its scope


A historical pattern is not a measured forecast. This guide provides no investment-return result or product-accuracy percentage. Evaluate the extraction and calculations on representative reports before relying on a larger workflow.
